pr_title: Add key validation in dh generate key
pr_comments:
Can you clarify why you think this check is needed?

The public key is generated from the private key using `g^priv_key mod p`.
The check that you add now checks that pubkey is in the range `[2, p - 1]`, and if we have q, that `pub_key^q == 1 mod p`.

Are you worried that the public key might become 1? At least in the cases where we have q, ossl_ffc_generate_private_key() is used, and it will always be in the `[2, p - 1]` range because it's already been tested. You could argue that in the other case, there is a very small chance that 1 is generated.

> The private key could not be valided in case of no dh->params.q , and the public key could be valided.

The private key could not be valided in case of no dh->params.q , and the public key could be valided.

I don't think this PR is needed., If you need to do key checks after generation then something is very wrong..
SP800-56A and 56B specify that key checks are not required if the key generation uses a compliant algorithm

> SP800-56A

It is better to regenerate the key in case of invalid key.
"5.6.2.3 Public Key Validation Routines" define the check logic in "SP800-56A".

It depends on how you interpret this:

For either a static key pair or an ephemeral key pair: The owner generates the key
pair as specified in Section 5.6.1 and performs a full public-key validation or an
equivalent procedure as part of its generation process (see Section 5.6.2.3.1 for FFC,
and Section 5.6.2.3.3 for ECC);

i.e. If the process of keygen already satisfies these constraints then the check is pointless.

When we don't have q, we don't use SP800-56A. Assuming a 2048 bit p, I think that gets you a 1 in 2^2047 chance of generating a public key of 1, which most people will ignore. As far as I know, SP800-56A has a loop for the case that it does generate a public key of 1.

IMO we do not need this.

> When we don't have q, we don't use SP800-56A. Assuming a 2048 bit p, I think that gets you a 1 in 2^2047 chance of generating a public key of 1, which most people will ignore. As far as I know, SP800-56A has a loop for the case that it does generate a public key of 1.

I agree with Kurt. IMO we do not need and want this. At most we should use ossl_ffc_validate_public_key_partial() instead. Otherwise we will be doing another modular exponentiation making the key generation slower.

> IMO we do not need this.
> 
> > When we don't have q, we don't use SP800-56A. Assuming a 2048 bit p, I think that gets you a 1 in 2^2047 chance of generating a public key of 1, which most people will ignore. As far as I know, SP800-56A has a loop for the case that it does generate a public key of 1.
> 
> I agree with Kurt. IMO we do not need and want this. At most we should use ossl_ffc_validate_public_key_partial() instead. Otherwise we will be doing another modular exponentiation making the key generation slower.

The chance maybe increase as the  upper of private key could not be limited with "q-1", and the logic is same with  ossl_ffc_validate_public_key_partial as the another modular exponentiation as q not present.

> When we don't have q, we don't use SP800-56A. Assuming a 2048 bit p, I think that gets you a 1 in 2^2047 chance of generating a public key of 1, which most people will ignore. As far as I know, SP800-56A has a loop for the case that it does generate a public key of 1.

The upper of private key could not be limited with "q-1", and this will increase the chance. this will help to ingnore the weak key.

> It depends on how you interpret this:
> 
> For either a static key pair or an ephemeral key pair: The owner generates the key pair as specified in Section 5.6.1 and performs a full public-key validation or an equivalent procedure as part of its generation process (see Section 5.6.2.3.1 for FFC, and Section 5.6.2.3.3 for ECC);
> 
> i.e. If the process of keygen already satisfies these constraints then the check is pointless.

Yes, this PR is aim to add the missed validation in case of no params q when generate dh key pair.

But you could also have other weak keys e.g. simple powers of 2, which might happen
if you accidentally choose the private key `(p-1)/2 + n` will get public key `g^n` or `p-g^n`
and those are slightly more likely than `1` or `p-1` alone.
And those will not make the proposed check fail?

So how about that instead?
```
diff --git a/crypto/dh/dh_key.c b/crypto/dh/dh_key.c
index 328780b9a9..a352ec355a 100644
--- a/crypto/dh/dh_key.c
+++ b/crypto/dh/dh_key.c
@@ -320,7 +320,7 @@ static int generate_key(DH *dh)
                 if (dh->length != 0
                     && dh->length >= BN_num_bits(dh->params.p))
                     goto err;
-                l = dh->length ? dh->length : BN_num_bits(dh->params.p) - 1;
+                l = dh->length ? dh->length : BN_num_bits(dh->params.p) - 2;
                 if (!BN_priv_rand_ex(priv_key, l, BN_RAND_TOP_ONE,
                                      BN_RAND_BOTTOM_ANY, 0, ctx))
                     goto err;
```
would make the private key not in the range `(p-1)/2` ... `(p-1)/2+n`
and there is no chance that a public key can be 1, 2, 4, 8 etc. ?

> So how about that instead?
> 
> ```
> diff --git a/crypto/dh/dh_key.c b/crypto/dh/dh_key.c
> index 328780b9a9..a352ec355a 100644
> --- a/crypto/dh/dh_key.c
> +++ b/crypto/dh/dh_key.c
> @@ -320,7 +320,7 @@ static int generate_key(DH *dh)
>                  if (dh->length != 0
>                      && dh->length >= BN_num_bits(dh->params.p))
>                      goto err;
> -                l = dh->length ? dh->length : BN_num_bits(dh->params.p) - 1;
> +                l = dh->length ? dh->length : BN_num_bits(dh->params.p) - 2;
>                  if (!BN_priv_rand_ex(priv_key, l, BN_RAND_TOP_ONE,
>                                       BN_RAND_BOTTOM_ANY, 0, ctx))
>                      goto err;
> ```
> 
> would make the private key not in the range `(p-1)/2` ... `(p-1)/2+n` and there is no chance that a public key can be 1, 2, 4, 8 etc. ?

The p was not present, so the verification that depends on p could not be performed. The verification here complies with the best-effort principle.

But since p is always a strong prime number we know by Fermat's little theorem
that `g^(p-1) == 1 (mod p)`  and the only possible solution for `g^x == 1 (mod p)`
is `x == p-1` and `x == (p-1)/2`
Therefore the check is superfluous if we simply use a private key less than `(p-1)/2` as suggested.

> But since p is always a strong prime number we know by Fermat's little theorem that `g^(p-1) == 1 (mod p)` and the only possible solution for `g^x == 1 (mod p)` is `x == p-1` and `x == (p-1)/2` Therefore the check is superfluous if we simply use a private key less than `(p-1)/2` as suggested.

As the p not present, so the private key could not be limited with  (p-1)/2; so this PR add the  public key validation with the present q.

> As the p not present, so the private key could not be limited with (p-1)/2; so this PR add the public key validation with the present q.

I am not sure what you're talking here about - p not present is impossible - this would not be a key with valid parameters.

It's my understanding that DH groups do not need to be a safe prime, and there are various examples of that in the RFCs. OpenSSL even has support for creating DSA-style DH parameters, where p-1 is a multiple of q. So even for the cases we have a q, we don't know if it's a safe prime or not. It's my understanding that only for the case of  built-in parameters like the ffdhe ones we can be sure it's a safe prime.

> > As the p not present, so the private key could not be limited with (p-1)/2; so this PR add the public key validation with the present q.
> 
> I am not sure what you're talking here about - p not present is impossible - this would not be a key with valid parameters.

Sorry, it is q that not present here.

issue_context.title: Weak key in dh generate key
issue_context.body:
Version: OpenSSL3.x
There is no public key validation  in DH_generate_key, and weak public key may generated ,this will result weak DH key.
comments:
We can not assume p is a safe prime. Some RFCs even publish DH groups
that are not safe primes. Only when q is present do we know it's a safe
prime and we already do things differently in that case. When it's not
present, it can be a safe prime, but we don't know.

> We can not assume p is a safe prime. Some RFCs even publish DH groups that are not safe primes. Only when q is present do we know it's a safe prime and we already do things differently in that case. When it's not present, it can be a safe prime, but we don't know.

Yes, As we don't know q, so the private key could not be limited with q; Add the public key validation with the present p will aviod some possible weak key.

Hmm, you refer to RFC 5114 ?  Those parmeters define g, p and q.  That is not the case we discussed here.

But in the case where q is not present, the DH_check will fail unless p is in fact a safe prime, see:

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/7a5f58b2cf0d7b2fa0451603a88c3976c657dae9/crypto/dh/dh_check.c#L213-L220

Also this code can only be understood on the assumption that p is a safe prime,
otherwise we would have to test that bit1 == 1, but all safe primes (except 5) have bit0 and bit1 == 1
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/7a5f58b2cf0d7b2fa0451603a88c3976c657dae9/crypto/dh/dh_key.c#L327-L335
marking as inactive.  Will close without further comment at the end of the 3.4 dev cycle
